description:
One-shot operator-only backfill that fills the `session_vendor` + `source_kind` columns on pre-migration `session_ledger__event` rows. SQL-lockdown #0 Slice 7 (Architect-ruled denormalize) added those two columns to `__event` so `list_events_by_source_window` reads a single table instead of a 3-table JOIN (event → session → source). `append_event` writes both on every NEW event going forward, so this verb only fills rows that predate the migration — until they are filled, the migrated single-table read silently drops them from `source_kind` / `vendor`-filtered pulls (a NULL column never matches an equality filter).

Properties. (1) Idempotent + fill-only: each pass updates ONLY events whose `session_vendor IS NULL`, and never overwrites a populated value — a re-run is a no-op. Because it is non-destructive there is no `confirm` gate (unlike the destructive repair verbs). (2) Fail-loud: a session whose `source_id` resolves to no live `__source` row (or whose `vendor` is NULL) raises `LedgerRepositoryError` and STOPS the backfill — the original INNER JOIN would have dropped those events, so a NULL `source_kind` fill would wrongly leak them into vendor-only pulls. This is a tripwire; it is unreachable in practice (`__source` rows are never soft-deleted, `vendor` is NOT NULL). (3) Bounded memory: driven by SESSIONS (orders of magnitude fewer than events), paged by an `id` keyset; each session is ONE server-side `update_state` over its own events, so the multi-million-row event corpus is never materialized. (4) Race-free with ongoing ingest: new events are born with `session_vendor` set, so the `IS NULL` filter never overlaps a live writer — no importer-poll pause is needed.

When to use. Run once after the Slice-7 schema adoption (the new columns land via the metadata-DDL schema-diff on the next install) to populate historical events. Re-run to confirm convergence — a clean run returns `events_denormalized` 0.

This verb is `is_discoverable=False` — the model cannot find it via process_search and never proposes it. Operator-only via the operator bridge.
embedding_description: Operator-only one-shot ledger backfill: fill session_vendor + source_kind on pre-migration __event rows from the authoritative session->source join (SQL-lockdown Slice 7 denormalization). append_event writes both on new events; this fills historical rows so list_events_by_source_window's single-table read doesn't drop them. Idempotent fill-NULL (no confirm gate), fail-loud on unresolved source, session-driven id-keyset paging, race-free with ingest. Returns sessions_scanned + events_denormalized.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Backfill counts. `sessions_scanned` is the number of `__session` rows visited (id-keyset paged); `events_denormalized` is the number of `__event` rows whose NULL `session_vendor` + `source_kind` were filled this run (0 on a converged ledger — re-run to confirm completeness).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a run, re-issue `list_events_by_source_window` with a `source_kind` / `vendor` filter over a historical window and confirm pre-migration events now appear. Re-run this verb to confirm `events_denormalized` is 0 (converged). If it ever raises `LedgerRepositoryError` about an unresolved source, that is a data anomaly — a `__session` row referencing a missing `__source` — investigate via `list_sources` before re-running.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Session-driven id-keyset pass over `__session`; per session, one predicated `update_state` fills `__event.session_vendor` + `source_kind` from the session's `vendor` + its source's `source_kind` where `session_vendor IS NULL`.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: LedgerRepositoryError: either a session's `source_id` resolved to no live `__source` row / its `vendor` was NULL (fail-loud data anomaly — the backfill stops rather than write a leaky NULL `source_kind`), or the underlying state_service rejected a read/UPDATE. Possible causes: schema not yet adopted (the new columns absent), a dangling `__session.source_id`, state_service unavailable.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Confirm the Slice-7 schema columns are present (adopted on the last install). For an unresolved-source anomaly, find the offending session via `list_sources` + `get_session_timeline` and reconcile the dangling `source_id` before re-running. The backfill is idempotent, so a re-run after fixing the anomaly resumes cleanly (already-filled events are skipped).
